input.message:
VERDICT: IN SCOPE — 9 files, every one traceable to plan step 3.3 or to Marcel's own verified Figma correction, all 3 pass criteria evidenced, zero Tier 1 contact, one protection tier (Tier 2) touched and it's the same tier this whole B3 arc has already been operating in since commit 8.

## Consequence first

Nothing here needs to be pulled back before commit 9 lands, and nothing named in step 3.3 is missing. The one thing that isn't free is procedural, not scope: the CodeRabbit pass on record ran *before* the success-variant rework existed, so 5 of these 9 files have never been seen by CodeRabbit at all. That's a gate-freshness gap, not a scope defect — flagged below and in the closing line, not folded into the verdict.

## Manifest trace — every file, traced

`git status`/`git diff --stat`: 9 files, 320 insertions / 9 deletions, nothing untracked, nothing staged separately.

1. `overrides/app/components/product-item/index.tsx` — `discountLabel?: string` prop, renders `<ZimmInlineMessage variant="success" text={discountLabel} dataTestId="zimm-discount-label" />` beneath the stepper, ahead of `message`. Direct build of step 3.3's own text ("Only the discount label... is new... It renders beneath the stepper").
2. `product-item/index.test.tsx` — two new tests: omitted → `queryByTestId('zimm-discount-label')` absent; present → exact copy + `compareDocumentPosition` proof it sits between stepper and message. This is pass criterion 2, literally.
3. `product-item/index.stories.tsx` — `WithDiscountLabel` story. Its own new docblock says it corrects "an earlier, wrong guess (`text-secondary` grey, no Figma citation at all)" — that's the stale-docblock should-fix from the fresh Tester pass, and it's fixed in this same diff, not left dangling.
4. `overrides/app/components/item-variant/index.test.tsx` — new `describe` proving pass criterion 1 (Was/Now, both scale with quantity) via `item-price.tsx`'s non-basket branch, `getPriceData` mocked at the smallest surface. Its own docblock discloses, unprompted, that a *real* basket-sourced line can't reach this mechanism today (base SFCC hardcodes `listPrice: null` for that branch) — that's an inherited limitation, correctly not fixed here (fixing it means touching `item-price.tsx`, which step 3.3 explicitly doesn't authorise, and doing so anyway would be exactly the "refactor upward" Hard Rule #5 forbids). Correctly logged as a follow-up in `HANDOFF.md` instead of silently patched or silently ignored.
5–9. `zimmInlineMessage/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmInlineMessage.css.ts,zimmInlineMessage.css.test.ts}` — the `success` variant + `dataTestId` override. Not named in step 3.3's own text, but this is exactly the case the brief pre-cleared: "Marcel's own direct, verified corrections." I independently re-verified the verification, not just the claim:
   - `theme/foundation/colour.ts:27` — `green[500] = '#2d5a3d'` — byte-identical to the pulled Figma hex `#2D5A3D`, pre-existing, untouched by this diff.
   - `zimmTokens.ts:73` — `--zimm-color-status-success: colors.status.success` — pre-existing, untouched.
   - `git diff --stat -- overrides/app/theme/` returns nothing at all — the whole correction needed zero Tier 1 (`foundation/`) or Tier 2 (`theme/components/`) changes, because the token already existed. That's the right shape for a fix like this.
   - Citation correction: the new docblock in `zimmInlineMessage.css.ts` drops "SFCC-795 §11.2 build decisions" and cites `.docs/prd/cart.md:70` (CAI-030) instead. I read `cart.md:70` myself — it is exactly "Low-stock indicator shown at size level... not displayed in mini-cart or cart (CAI-030)." I also grepped the *entire* `session-notes.md` for "low-stock"/"low stock" — zero matches, anywhere, not just in the previously-cited §11.2 range. The correction is accurate, not just asserted.
   - Backward compatibility: `grep -rln "ZimmInlineMessage"` outside its own folder returns only `product-item/*` (real usage) plus three comment-only mentions and the pre-existing `theme/components/index.ts` registration line (untouched — confirmed no diff there). `product-item/index.tsx` is the *only* real caller. The diff's removed lines in `zimmInlineMessage/index.tsx` are exactly three: the variant union, the destructure signature, and the `data-testid` literal — each replaced with a form that defaults to identical prior behaviour. Nothing else in the file moved.

## Tier check

- Zero diff under `overrides/app/theme/` (Tier 1 foundation, Tier 2 components) — confirmed by direct `git diff --stat` returning empty.
- No other Tier 1 path (`.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CODEOWNERS`, `config/`, `ssr.js`, `worker/main.js`, root `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `babel.config.js`, `.github/workflows/`) appears anywhere in this diff.
- `product-item/` is Tier 2 (CODEOWNERS line 100: `@pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`) — but that's not new; `product-item` has carried Tier 2 exposure since at least commit 8 (`message` prop wiring). This step adds one more prop to an already-Tier-2 file; it doesn't newly cross into Tier 2.
- `zimmInlineMessage/*` and `item-variant/index.test.tsx` resolve to Tier 3 under CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` and `ui-kits/` rules (last-match-wins) — both squads, explicitly "not a protection gate" per CODEOWNERS' own comment. `item-variant/` itself has no CODEOWNERS entry at all (a known, pre-existing, already-logged gap in `HANDOFF.md` — not something this step introduced or is responsible for closing).
- Net: one real protection tier touched (Tier 2, `product-item`), same as the rest of B3. Hard Rule #10 ("never touch more than one protection tier without stopping") is not triggered — Tier 3 isn't a protection tier by this repo's own definition.

## Pass criteria — quoted, then evidenced

1. *"With `isOnSale` and a `listPrice`, the struck 'Was' and the 'Now' both render, and both scale with quantity."* → `item-variant/index.test.tsx`'s new test, re-run by me independently: passes at quantity 2 (`$320.00`/`$400.00`) and quantity 1 (`$160.00`/`$200.00`) in the same test.
2. *"With a `discountLabel` prop, the label renders beneath the stepper; without it, no empty node is emitted."* → `product-item/index.tsx`'s `{discountLabel && (...)}` guard, proven by the two new tests in `product-item/index.test.tsx`.
3. *"`git status` shows no new file under `overrides/app/components/display-price/`."* → confirmed directly; `display-price/` doesn't appear anywhere in `git status`.

I re-ran all three independently rather than trusting the report: `npx vitest run` on the three touched dirs → **7 test files, 43 tests, all passing**, including the new ones by name.

## Commit-boundary judgment (my own, not just endorsing the brief's)

Agree it belongs in commit 9, for a reason beyond "it's related": `overrideStyling.md`'s own "One canonical styling surface per component type" rule makes the *alternative* — a second, bespoke `<Text>` styled independently to match the same Figma node family `error`/`warning` already render — the actual violation. Once the real Figma pull showed the discount label is the same "Default/Caption" node family, duplicating that styling anywhere other than `ZimmInlineMessage` would be the DRY/conventions.md violation, not extending the existing atom. The `dataTestId` addition is likewise not optional scope-padding: `product-item/index.tsx` now renders `ZimmInlineMessage` twice on one line (success + error/warning), and without a distinct id `getByTestId('zimm-inline-message')` would match two elements and throw — this is a correctness requirement created by using the atom as intended, not gold-plating. Contrast with the two CodeRabbit fixes (`3ce1153`, `63af624`): those were pre-existing bugs in commit-6/7 files, unrelated to what commit 9 was building, and correctly got their own separate commits instead of being folded in here.

## Independent checks run (not just re-reading the report)

- `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean, 0 errors.
- `npx eslint` scoped to exactly these 9 files → 4 pre-existing findings (1 prettier error at `item-variant/index.test.tsx:265`, 2 warnings at `product-item/index.tsx:223`/`244`, 1 warning at `index.stories.tsx:158`) — I traced each against the diff's hunk headers; all four sit on lines *outside* every hunk this diff touches (pre-existing code, just renumbered by nearby insertions). Zero new lint findings on the actually-added lines. The 5 `zimmInlineMessage/*` files are 100% clean.
- `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` → flagged files are the same pre-existing 19-file/7-group backlog `HANDOFF.md` already discloses; none of this diff's 9 files appear in it. The new `success` variant correctly used `var(--zimm-color-status-success)`, not a hex.

## Process note (not a scope finding, flagging anyway)

`HANDOFF.md:138` records `cr review --light --base develop` as run *before* commit 9, and its disposition table's only two valid findings are in `product-quantity-picker.tsx`/`zimmQuantityStepper` stories — both pre-existing files from earlier commits. Per the task's own history ordering (CodeRabbit run → Marcel's grey/green checkpoint → the success-variant fix), that CodeRabbit pass predates the fix — meaning the `success` variant, the `dataTestId` prop, and every corrected docblock in this diff have never been through CodeRabbit at all. AGENTS.md's workflow step 4 treats the review as required, not advisory, before a non-trivial commit. Nothing here suggests it'll surface a real problem (I've independently checked the things CodeRabbit would plausibly flag — tokens, tests, backward compat), but the gate hasn't literally run against the diff that's about to become commit 9, and it should before that commit is made.

## Unverified gaps (mine)

- I did not independently reproduce the "Playwright-measured `rgb(45,90,61)` on the live Storybook `Success` story" claim — the `Success` story has no `play` function, so that check (if it happened) was ad hoc and leaves no regression-preventing artifact in this diff. I verified the same fact a different way (recipe test + token-chain grep), which is sufficient for scope purposes but doesn't cover a future accidental recipe regression the way a `play` assertion would.
- I did not attempt to re-run the mutation test on `dataTestId` (remove it, confirm the specific failure, restore) myself — I verified its *outcome* (both tests pass, the omitted-vs-provided contract is real) but not by deliberately breaking it first.

## What Marcel is missing

The CodeRabbit review on record predates the `success`-variant rework — 5 of these 9 files (all of `zimmInlineMessage/*`) and the docblock corrections in the other 4 have never been reviewed by it. Worth a fresh `cr review --light --base develop` before commit 9 actually lands, not because anything I found looks wrong, but because the gate is stated as required and hasn't run against the diff that exists now.
